paper.title: FrontierCS 2: A Benchmark for Computer Science R&D
paper.abstract: Can LLM agents make contributions to frontier computer science R&D? We introduce FrontierCS 2, a benchmark of 48 open-ended tasks. We take a paper and the code its authors released and delete the paper's contribution. The deleted code becomes the human reference that sets the bar. Earlier open-ended benchmarks give each agent a problem statement and grade one program after the run. FrontierCS 2 places the agent inside a research environment. The agent inherits a working repository and may submit

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要回答的问题不是“模型能不能做代码题”，而是“LLM agent 能不能在真实研究仓库里，基于已有系统做出接近论文贡献级别的改进”。作者认为现有 open-ended benchmark 大多给一个题目、收一个最终程序、做一次离线评分，这和真实计算机科学研发差得很远。真实研发更像是在一个可运行仓库上删掉某个关键创新，再要求研究者把它补回来并超过原实现。论文的核心问题就是如何把这种研发过程做成一个可评测、可保密、又尽量贴近真实研究环境的 benchmark。
summary.importance: 对基座研究本身，它不是预训练方法论文，但对 post-train agent 能力评估有较强参考价值，尤其适合关注 coding agent、research agent、以及“模型能力是否真的接近研发自动化”的团队。它的重要性主要来自 benchmark 设计，而不是某个新模型结果。第一，任务构造方式比常见 benchmark 更接近真实研发闭环：继承代码库、局部编辑、反复提交 patch、拿开发集反馈、最后在隐藏测试上定稿。第二，评分标准不是 rubric，也不是公开 leaderboard，而是和论文作者原始实现直接对比，这让“超过人类参考实现”有了更硬的含义。第三，作者给出能力指数 FCI 和任务难度指数，试图把不同 agent、不同预算、不同任务放到同一尺度上比较。对做 agent post-training 或 tool-use 训练的人，这类 benchmark 能更早暴露出模型在长期搜索、实验管理、局部修改约束、以及 final patch selection 上的短板。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是“tasks built by subtraction”。作者从论文作者公开的代码仓库出发，定位实现论文贡献的那部分代码，将其删除，但保留其余依赖和调用接口不变。agent 拿到的是一个仍然能运行、但关键贡献被挖空的仓库，需要只在指定文件中补回缺失实现。被删除的原始代码作为 private human reference，由 judge 保管，不暴露给 agent。这样做的好处有两个：一是任务天然有 oracle reference，不需要人工重写标准答案；二是 agent 面对的是研究者真实会遇到的“在现有系统上做增量创新”场景，而不是从零写一个程序。

Judge 设计也比较讲究。agent 和 judge 分处不同 sandbox，agent 无法联网下载原仓库历史或作者代码，只能通过 driver 调用模型和提交 patch。judge 持有 evaluator、held-out final suite 和 human reference。运行过程中，agent 可以多次提交 patch，judge 只返回 development suite 上的阈值达成情况和简化分数，不暴露参考实现分数或 evaluator 原始输出。最终成绩只看 agent 自己选定的 final patch 在 held-out suite 上是否在每个 metric、每个 workload 上都超过 reference 设定阈值。这个设计避免了 agent 直接对测试集过拟合，也把“何时停止、选哪个版本提交”纳入能力评估。

论文还引入 FrontierCS Capabilities Index（FCI）和匹配的 difficulty index，用来在单一尺度上比较 agent 与任务。虽然从提供内容看不到完整建模细节，但它显然不是简单 pass@1，而是试图做类似项目反应理论那样的能力-难度联合拟合。对于 benchmark 研究，这是比单纯排行榜更有解释力的一步。
summary.experiments:
实验覆盖 48 个任务、13 个领域、12 个模型/agent 组合，每个任务只跑一遍。最强组合是 Claude Opus 5.5 配 Claude Code，pass rate 为 58%；其余 agent 都低于 50%。还有一个很说明问题的结果：16 个任务没有任何 agent 通过。这说明 benchmark 不是靠少数极难任务拉开差距，而是存在一批当前主流 agent 普遍做不动的研发型任务。

任务通过标准也比较严格：不是单一指标超过即可，而是必须在 held-out suite 的每个 metric、每个 workload 上都超过 human reference 的阈值。以文中举的 SVG-EAR 为例，延迟需不高于 reference 的 0.96 倍，同时 PSNR、SSIM、LPIPS 还要维持在给定容忍范围内。这种多指标门槛更接近真实系统研究里的 trade-off，而不是只拼一个 leaderboard 数字。

作者还分析了 cost budget 对领先 agent 的影响，说明 benchmark 不只是测“单次最强模型”，也能测预算-能力曲线。由于提供内容不含完整表格，这里不能补充更多具体模型排名或 FCI 数值，但已有信息足够说明：当前顶级 coding/research agent 在真实仓库研发环境中仍远未稳定达到“重建并超过论文贡献”的水平。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读时先看 Introduction 和 task construction。关键不是记住 48 个任务，而是理解 subtraction-based task building 为什么比传统题目式 benchmark 更贴近研发。然后看 Judge 设计，特别是 agent/judge 信息隔离、development suite 与 held-out final suite 的分工、以及 final patch 由 agent 自己选择这一点。接着看主结果图：pass rate、哪些任务无人通过、FCI 与 difficulty index 的拟合。最后再看 case studies，判断失败主要来自算法设计、实验搜索、工程调参，还是长时程决策。

预计 25 到 40 分钟可以完成一次有效泛读。如果你关心 agent post-training 或 benchmark 设计，建议额外看附录里的任务来源表和评分细则，重点检查任务是否真的覆盖不同 CS 子领域，以及阈值设置是否会偏向某类系统。阅读时值得带着两个问题：一是“删掉论文贡献再补回”是否会低估真正从零提出新想法的难度；二是单次运行设置会不会把 agent 的方差和 harness 差异混在一起。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自 Georgia Institute of Technology、University of Wisconsin–Madison、University of Pennsylvania 等机构。提供内容中可见作者包括 Qiuyang Mang、Wenhao Chai、Hanchen Li 等；完整作者与机构映射在截取文本里不完整。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper asks a harder question than standard coding benchmarks: can an LLM agent operate inside a real research repository and reproduce, then surpass, the contribution of a published computer science paper? Existing open-ended benchmarks usually provide a problem statement, collect one final program, and score it once after the run. That setup misses much of actual R&D, where a researcher inherits a working codebase, modifies a specific component, runs experiments repeatedly, and decides which patch to submit. FrontierCS 2 is designed to benchmark that workflow rather than isolated code generation.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining paper, but it is relevant to post-training and agent evaluation because it measures a capability frontier that many coding-agent claims do not really test: iterative research work in a live repository under hidden evaluation. Its main value lies in benchmark design. First, the tasks are grounded in real published systems rather than synthetic prompts. Second, success is defined against the authors’ own implementation, not a rubric or a public leaderboard. Third, the benchmark includes a capability index and a difficulty index, aiming to compare agents and tasks on a common scale instead of relying only on raw pass rates. For teams working on coding agents, tool use, or research automation, this benchmark is a useful stress test for long-horizon search, patch selection, and constrained editing in realistic environments.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The central construction is 'tasks built by subtraction.' Starting from a released research repository, the benchmark builders identify the code that implements the paper’s contribution, delete it, and leave the rest of the repository intact. The deleted code becomes a private human reference held by the judge. The agent receives the modified repository, where the missing functions are still declared and called, and is allowed to edit only the files that originally contained the contribution. This gives each task a natural oracle reference without requiring benchmark authors to manually recreate a gold solution.

The judge design is equally important. The agent and the judge run in separate sandboxes. The agent has no network access beyond a driver that forwards model calls and patch submissions, preventing trivial recovery of the original code. The judge holds the evaluator, the held-out final suite, and the private reference patch. During the run, the agent may submit patches multiple times and receives only development-suite feedback: simplified scores and threshold counts, not raw evaluator outputs or reference scores. At the end, the agent must choose one final patch, and only that patch is evaluated on the held-out suite. A run passes only if the final patch beats the reference threshold on every metric and every held-out workload. This setup makes patch selection part of the task and reduces direct overfitting to the final evaluation.

The paper also introduces the FrontierCS Capabilities Index (FCI) together with a task difficulty index. While the provided text does not include the full fitting details, the intent is clear: estimate agent capability and task difficulty jointly on a single latent scale, rather than treating benchmark performance as a flat leaderboard.
summary_en.experiments:
The benchmark contains 48 tasks across 13 domains and evaluates 12 model-plus-agent-harness combinations, with one run per task. The best-performing setup, Claude Opus 5.5 with Claude Code, passes 58% of runs. Every other agent passes fewer than half. An especially informative result is that no agent passes 16 of the tasks. That suggests the benchmark is not merely separating agents with a few outlier tasks; there is a substantial subset of research-style tasks that current top agents broadly fail.

The pass criterion is intentionally strict. Success is not defined by a single scalar score but by meeting thresholds on every metric and every held-out workload. In the SVG-EAR example described in the text, latency must be at most 0.96 times the reference latency while PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS must remain within specified tolerances of the reference. This better reflects real systems research, where improvements usually have to satisfy multiple constraints simultaneously.

The paper also studies how the leading agent changes with the cost budget per run, which makes the benchmark useful for scaling analyses rather than only one-shot ranking. The provided excerpt does not include the full result tables or exact FCI values, so it would be inappropriate to invent finer-grained rankings. Still, the reported numbers already support a clear conclusion: current frontier coding/research agents are far from reliably reconstructing and outperforming paper-level contributions in realistic repository environments.
summary_en.reading_guide:
For a skim, start with the introduction and the task-building section. The key idea to understand is why subtraction-based construction is closer to real R&D than prompt-only coding tasks. Then read the judge section carefully, especially the separation between agent and judge, the role of the development suite versus the held-out final suite, and the fact that the agent must choose its own final patch. After that, go to the main results: pass rates, the set of tasks that no agent solves, and the FCI/difficulty analysis. If available, finish with the case studies to see whether failures are driven more by algorithm design, experiment search, engineering constraints, or long-horizon decision making.

A useful skim should take about 25–40 minutes. If your interest is benchmark design or agent post-training, spend extra time on the appendix tables listing task sources and scoring thresholds. Two good questions to keep in mind are whether 'delete and rebuild the contribution' understates the difficulty of originating a new idea from scratch, and whether the one-run-per-task protocol mixes model capability with harness variance too strongly.
summary_en.authors_note: The visible affiliations include Georgia Institute of Technology, University of Wisconsin–Madison, and University of Pennsylvania. The excerpt shows authors such as Qiuyang Mang, Wenhao Chai, and Hanchen Li, but the full author–affiliation mapping is incomplete in the provided text.

recommendation.zh: 读任务构造和隐藏评分协议即可；它是 agent 研发能力的好压力测试，但不是训练方法论文。
recommendation.en: Read the task construction and hidden-scoring protocol; it is a useful stress test for R&D agents, not a training-method paper.

paper.title: Recursive Self-Improvement on a Budget: Scoring Code Edits Before They Run
paper.abstract: A coding agent that rewrites its own scaffold has to choose which proposed edit to expand before that edit has been evaluated, and the search then has to return one agent. Each run fits one linear readout on the parent's steering-split solve rate and eight coordinates of the proposed diff, from 96 scaffold edits labeled by four evaluations of a 16-instance fit split, and then freezes the coefficients. HumanEval+ reserves 48 instances as the steering split and Polyglot reserves 64. That split sco

summary.core_problem: 论文研究预算受限的自改进 coding agent 如何在运行评测前选择要扩展的 scaffold edit。问题不是代码生成本身，而是搜索过程中对候选 diff 的预评估：哪些修改值得花一次昂贵的 checker evaluation。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接影响有限，更多属于 agent scaffold search 和自动化程序改写的经验方法。与基座训练相关的启发在于，它把“生成候选—用小模型或线性读出器预筛—再花预算评测”的思路用于 agent 自改进。这类机制和数据筛选、RL 训练中的 verifier 预算分配有相似结构，但论文实验规模较小，结论主要适合作为低成本搜索策略参考。
summary.technical_approach: 方法是在每次搜索前拟合一个冻结的线性 surrogate。特征由两部分组成：父节点在 steering split 上的 solve rate，以及候选 unified diff 的 8 维随机投影 embedding。diff 先用 text-embedding-3-small 得到 1536 维向量，再用每次 run 独立采样的随机高斯投影压到 8 维；加上父节点分数后形成 9 维特征。校准阶段生成 96 个 scaffold edits，并用 16 个 fit instances、每个 edit 4 次评测得到标签，然后最小二乘拟合线性读出器。搜索阶段保留 4 个已评估节点的 archive，每个 keep step 生成 8 个 proposals，读出器在运行前打分，只扩展最高分候选。对照方法包括只用父节点 solve rate 的线性 ablation，以及 Huxley–Gödel Machine selection：后者对已评估节点的 steering success/failure counts 采样 Beta(1+n_s, 1+n_f)，选择采样值最大的父节点扩展其 child。
summary.experiments: 实验使用 HumanEval+ 和 Polyglot。HumanEval+ 中，steering split 为 48 个实例，held-out split 为 100 个实例；Polyglot 中，steering split 为 64 个实例，held-out split 为 145 个实例。每个 run 中，readout 和 parent-rate ablation 先标注 96 个 calibration edits，再进行 24 个 keep steps。Huxley–Gödel Machine selection 在 Polyglot 上扩展 144 个 children，在 HumanEval+ 上扩展 176 个 children。生成器包括 Claude Sonnet 4.5 和 GPT-4o，分别在不同 benchmark 上拟合。正文说明 Table 1 报告返回节点的 held-out score，Table 2 报告首个 keep step 选择的 child，Figure 1 展示返回节点；可见信息中明确提到 GPT-4o 在 HumanEval+ 上 readout 返回节点优于 parent-rate ablation。具体 held-out 数值在给定内容中未列出，因此不应过度外推。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读方法和实验设置，预计 20 到 30 分钟。重点看三个细节：一是 96 个 calibration edits 如何构造，二是 diff embedding 的随机 8 维投影是否稳定，三是 readout 与 parent-rate ablation 的差异是否主要来自 diff 特征。若只关心基座模型训练，可跳过 theorem 证明；Beta posterior draw 的均值公式较直接，核心信息是它把父节点选择写成基于 steering counts 的 Thompson sampling。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies how a self-modifying coding agent should choose scaffold edits before paying for evaluator runs. The central question is pre-evaluation ranking of proposed diffs under a fixed checker budget, not general code generation quality.
summary_en.importance: The work is only loosely connected to foundation-model pretraining. Its relevance is in budget allocation for agent improvement: generate several candidate edits, score them with a cheap surrogate, and evaluate only one. This resembles verifier-guided filtering and data selection pipelines, but the experiments are small and centered on coding-agent scaffolds. It is best read as an empirical note on low-cost search control rather than as a general agent-training result.
summary_en.technical_approach: The method fits a frozen linear readout before search. Each candidate diff is represented by the parent node’s steering-split solve rate plus eight random-projection coordinates of the diff embedding. The diff is embedded with text-embedding-3-small into 1536 dimensions, then projected by a run-specific random Gaussian matrix to 8 dimensions. Together with the parent score, this gives a 9-dimensional feature vector. The readout is trained by least squares on 96 calibration edits, each labeled by four evaluations on a fixed 16-instance fit split. During search, an archive keeps four evaluated nodes. At each keep step, eight proposals are generated across the archive, the readout scores them before execution, and only the highest-scoring edit is expanded. Baselines include a parent-rate-only ablation and Huxley–Gödel Machine selection, which samples from Beta(1+n_s, 1+n_f) using steering success and failure counts of evaluated nodes.
summary_en.experiments: The benchmarks are HumanEval+ and Polyglot. HumanEval+ uses 48 steering instances and 100 held-out instances. Polyglot uses 64 steering instances and 145 held-out instances. The readout and the parent-rate ablation spend 96 calibration labels and then run 24 keep steps. Huxley–Gödel Machine selection expands 144 children on Polyglot and 176 on HumanEval+. Claude Sonnet 4.5 and GPT-4o are fitted separately. The provided text states that Table 1 reports held-out scores, Table 2 shows the first-step child selected by the readout and ablation, and Figure 1 plots the returned node. It explicitly notes that on HumanEval+, GPT-4o’s returned node under the readout beats the parent-rate ablation. Exact held-out scores are not available in the supplied content.
summary_en.reading_guide: A quick 20–30 minute read is sufficient. Focus on the calibration protocol, the 9-feature linear readout, and the comparison against the parent-rate-only ablation. The useful question is whether the random-projected diff features add signal beyond simply expanding high-scoring parents. The theorem on the Beta draw can be skimmed; it mainly formalizes the mean of the Thompson-sampling parent selection rule.

recommendation.zh: 自改脚手架的 setup 小但问题干净；只看选择规则和 held-out 返回准则，别把小样本结论外推。
recommendation.en: The self-editing scaffold setup is small but clean; read the selection rule and held-out return criterion, but avoid over-reading the tiny-budget results.

paper.title: ExpEvolve: Structuring and Reusing Experience for Open-Ended Discovery
paper.abstract: Evolutionary coding agents such as AlphaEvolve are one of the notable successes in using Large Language Models (LLMs) to build AI Scientists. These agents tackle open-ended scientific problems by iteratively improving and evolving programs, leveraging the prior knowledge and reasoning capabilities of LLMs. Despite their success, mutations over programs are mostly low-level upon surface heuristics, without a persistent unit of control. In contrast, science compounds through ideas. In this work, w

summary.core_problem: 在开放式“进化式编码发现”（不断生成/变异程序、用外部评估器打分）的循环里，经验很难被有效复用：LLM 往往在低层细节（超参、实现微调）上做局部搜索，缺少能跨代累积的“想法/机制”级控制变量，导致探索效率低、容易陷入重复试错。论文要解决的是：如何从已评估的程序与分数中抽取可复用的高层 idea factors，并用它们来驱动后续探索-利用的决策。
summary.importance: 对预训练本身（数据/优化/recipe）不是直接贡献，更像是面向“AI scientist / 开放式发现”的 agent 搜索方法。但它给预训练研究的启发点在于：1）把“经验复用”从文本记忆/总结提升到可操作的因子化控制变量，类似把训练动态中的有效改动抽象成可复用的 recipe 片段；2）用可检验的判别任务（预测程序对的优劣）来筛选可用的高层因子，避免纯主观总结；3）用 bandit 做 idea 级调度，提供一种比启发式 mutation 更稳定的探索策略。整体属于可泛化的方法论启发，量级中等，偏 skim。
summary.technical_approach: 核心设计是“idea 抽取 + idea 控制”。(1) 形式化：把进化式发现写成 POMDP，隐藏状态是问题机制 θ_sci，动作是提出程序 p_t，观测是评估分数 y_t。定义 idea 为决定分数差异的高层机制属性（如构造家族、优化策略）。文中用定理刻画：不识别 idea 时，程序之间不可比较，搜索退化为近似穷举；而识别 idea 需要足够的对比性探索（有/无某 idea 的程序都要出现）。(2) idea factors 发现：在已评估程序档案上，寻找能解释“哪个程序更好”的高层因素。实现上基于 COAT（文中引用的框架），把候选因素当作可解释特征，目标是对任意程序对 (p_i, p_j) 预测哪一个分数更高；能稳定提升对比预测的因素被“admit”为 idea factor。这里的关键取舍是：用 pairwise ranking 作为训练/筛选信号，比直接回归分数更鲁棒，也更贴合“差异解释”。(3) idea-level 控制：把每个已发现的 idea factor 当作一个 bandit arm，在生成新候选程序时选择要强调/变异的 idea（利用），同时保留随机探索槽位；当搜索进入平台期时触发 idea-guided exploration，强制 LLM 去探索在当前 top 程序中不常见的 idea，以满足前述“对比性探索”的条件。整体上，它把进化搜索的控制粒度从 token/patch 级提升到“可复用的机制因子”级。
summary.experiments: 实验设置强调“小预算开放式发现”：在 11 个开放式数学发现任务上，总评估预算 200 个程序；两种代际划分：20 代×每代 10 个、10 代×每代 20 个。以 SCS 作为 backbone，并与 SCS、ShinkaEvolve 等对比。结果描述为：在多数设置下，ExpEvolve 在更小预算时取得更高最终 best-so-far，最高可到 5.0× 的提升（文中表述为 up to 5.0×，但给出的全文片段未包含逐任务绝对分数/方差，建议查 Sec.5 的主表）。分析实验包括：发现的 idea factors 在“对档案程序排序”上优于用代码长度等简单 proxy（11/11 任务）；把 ExpEvolve 集成进 OpenRSI，在 MLS-Bench 的 6 个任务上，mean final best-so-far 全部提升。若要判断稳健性，需要重点看：不同 seed 方差、bandit/探索策略消融、以及 idea factor 数量随时间的增长曲线（这些通常在分析小节/附录）。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议（约 25–35 分钟）：1）先看 Sec.3 的 POMDP 与 idea 定义，以及 Thm.3.1/3.3，理解作者为什么认为“没有 idea 就会退化为穷举”，以及为什么必须显式保证对比性探索；2）再看方法部分对 COAT 的用法：idea factor 的候选生成、pairwise 预测任务、admission 标准；3）最后看 Sec.5 主结果表与两个集成实验（OpenRSI/MLS-Bench），确认提升主要来自“idea 控制”还是“额外探索预算/plateau 触发”。如果只想拿走可迁移的工程做法：重点抄 bandit 调度 + plateau 触发的探索策略，以及用 pairwise ranking 来筛选可复用经验因子。

summary_en.core_problem: Open-ended evolutionary coding agents accumulate many scored programs, but they rarely reuse experience at the right abstraction level. LLM-guided mutations drift toward low-level tweaks and lack a persistent control unit comparable to human “ideas”. The paper targets a concrete gap: extract high-level idea factors from the archive of (program, score) pairs and use them as explicit control variables to steer exploration vs. exploitation in subsequent generations.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining-recipe paper; it sits in the AI-scientist / open-ended search space. Still, it offers transferable lessons for foundation-model researchers: (1) turn vague “memory” into actionable, factorized controls; (2) validate candidate abstractions with a discriminative, checkable signal (pairwise preference) rather than free-form summaries; (3) use bandit-style scheduling to manage competing hypotheses/recipes under tight evaluation budgets. Net impact is methodological and moderate; suitable for skimming unless you work on agentic discovery loops.
summary_en.technical_approach: The method is a two-stage loop: idea discovery and idea control. (1) Formalization: evolutionary discovery is cast as a POMDP with a hidden mechanism θ_sci; proposing a program yields a score from an evaluator. An “idea” is defined as a high-level mechanistic property of programs that causally drives score differences. The theory section argues that without identifying such ideas, programs are effectively unrelated and search degenerates toward exhaustive exploration; conversely, identifying ideas requires deliberate contrastive exploration (programs with/without an idea). (2) Idea-factor extraction: built on COAT, the system searches for high-level factors that explain score differences by training/using a pairwise comparator over archived programs—given (p_i, p_j), predict which scores higher. Factors that improve this pairwise ordering are admitted as reusable idea factors. The key design choice is pairwise ranking (difference-explaining) rather than raw score regression. (3) Idea-level control: each admitted idea factor becomes an arm in a multi-armed bandit that selects which idea to emphasize when generating new candidates. The algorithm reserves capacity for random exploration and triggers idea-guided exploration on plateaus, explicitly pushing the LLM toward underrepresented ideas in top programs to maintain the contrasts needed for reliable factor identification.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluation focuses on small-budget open-ended math discovery: 11 tasks, total budget 200 evaluated programs, with two generation layouts (20×10 and 10×20). Using SCS as the backbone and comparing against SCS and ShinkaEvolve, ExpEvolve improves final best-so-far in most settings; the paper reports gains up to 5.0× under smaller budgets (check Sec.5 tables for per-task absolute numbers and variance). Additional analyses show the discovered idea factors rank archived programs better than simple proxies like code length across all 11 tasks. Integrated into OpenRSI, ExpEvolve improves mean final best-so-far on all 6 MLS-Bench tasks used in that experiment. For rigor, the most important missing-from-snippet details to verify are seed variance, ablations on bandit/plateau triggers, and how many idea factors are admitted over time.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim plan (25–35 minutes): (1) Read the POMDP + idea definition and the key theorems in Sec.3 to understand the claimed failure mode (degenerating to brute-force) and the need for contrastive exploration. (2) Jump to the method section describing how COAT is used for pairwise ordering and the admission criterion for idea factors. (3) Scan Sec.5 main tables and the OpenRSI/MLS-Bench integration to attribute gains to idea control vs. extra exploration heuristics. If you want reusable engineering patterns, focus on: pairwise preference as a filter for reusable abstractions, and bandit scheduling with plateau-triggered diversification.

recommendation.zh: 不是 pretrain 论文，但“把经验压成可复用高层因子”这个接口值得借到 self-improving data generation；先看理论条件和 plateau 恢复实验。
recommendation.en: Not a pretraining paper, but the idea of compressing experience into reusable high-level factors may transfer to self-improving data generation; read the theory conditions and plateau-recovery results first.

paper.title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
paper.abstract: Moving from controllable videos to genuinely playable worlds requires persistent world state, executable game rules, and low-latency interaction. We outline a roadmap for the next generation of Matrix-Game that separates game execution from visual generation through an executable game harness, and introduce Matrix-Game 4.0 as the first system built on this design. A lightweight game engine maintains world state and executes interaction rules, a multimodal coding agent translates player ideas int

summary.core_problem: 把可控视频推进到可实时交互的游戏世界，需要同时解决持久世界状态、可执行规则和低延迟视觉生成的问题。
summary.importance: 贡献是一个交互式视频世界生成系统设计：把游戏逻辑执行和视觉生成拆开。它对 world model、交互式生成和 agent-生成模型接口有参考价值，但不是 LLM 基座预训练方法。
summary.technical_approach: Matrix-Game 4.0 使用轻量游戏引擎维护世界状态并执行交互规则；多模态 coding agent 将玩家自然语言想法转成游戏代码和动态场景 caption；自回归视频 renderer 将低模代理画面渲染为高保真视觉结果，并以动态 caption 和 memory reference 为条件。renderer 用低模—高保真对齐视频对训练，并蒸馏成 causal generator 以降低交互延迟。
summary.experiments: 摘要描述了系统训练与实时生成目标，但未给出模型参数量、数据规模、延迟数值、用户研究或与其他 playable world 系统的定量对比。

summary_en.core_problem: The work aims to move from controllable video generation to real-time playable worlds that require persistent state, executable rules, and low-latency interaction.
summary_en.importance: Its contribution is an interactive world-generation system that separates game execution from visual rendering. It is relevant to world models and agent-to-generator interfaces, but it is not a foundation-model pretraining method.
summary_en.technical_approach: Matrix-Game 4.0 uses a lightweight game engine to maintain world state and execute rules. A multimodal coding agent translates player intent into game code and dynamic scene captions. An autoregressive video renderer turns low-poly engine proxies into high-fidelity visuals conditioned on captions and memory references. The renderer is trained on aligned low-poly/high-fidelity video pairs and distilled into a causal generator for lower-latency interaction.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract describes the system and training setup but does not provide model size, data scale, latency numbers, user-study results, or quantitative comparisons against other playable-world systems.

recommendation.zh: 系统拆分思路比模型细节更有用；看架构图即可，别把它当 world model 预训练证据。
recommendation.en: The system decomposition is more useful than the model details; read the architecture, but do not treat it as evidence for world-model pretraining.

paper.title: REM: What to Store, When to Recall, What to Forget in Experience Memory for Coding Agents
paper.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents now autonomously complete long-horizon tasks, such as repository-level coding, through hundreds of think-act steps, yet the experience each run produces is rarely reused on the next. Prior memory systems concentrate on retrieval, finding the most relevant past trajectory. Retrieval cannot observe the running agent, so it cannot decide whether the agent needs an experience, at which point, or for how long. We introduce REM (Reusable Experience Memory), a framewor

summary.core_problem: 长时程 coding agent 会产生大量可复用的“经验轨迹”，但现有记忆系统多把问题简化为检索：找一条相关轨迹塞进上下文。论文要解决的是：经验复用失败往往不在检索命中率，而在记忆生命周期缺乏控制——该存什么形式、何时注入、注入后何时移除，才能在不干扰当前推理的前提下提升端到端修复成功率。
summary.importance:
对基座预训练本身不是直接贡献，但对“长上下文利用、持续学习式 agent、以及把轨迹变成训练/记忆资产”的研究很贴近。它给了几个对预训练/训练动态有启发的结论：
- 长上下文不是越多越好：注入位置与时机决定收益，错误时机会造成负迁移；这与 pretrain 时的长上下文课程、以及 post-train 时的工具轨迹蒸馏都有共性。
- 轨迹的“结构”比细节更可迁移：把一次 run 压缩成阶段化文档（localize/understand/fix/verify）能显著提升检索与复用效果，提示训练数据也许应更偏向结构化过程而非原始日志。
- 记忆是控制问题：是否需要经验、需要哪一层经验、持续多久，应由 in-loop 的状态观测来决策，而不是离线检索一次性决定。
整体属于 agent memory 方法论文，但它的实验把“上下文利用率低、长轨迹干扰推理、强模型更容易被多余记忆拖累”这些现象量化出来，值得基座研究员当作长上下文训练与数据形态设计的证据。
summary.technical_approach:
REM 把经验记忆拆成三个显式决策点，并把决策放到 agent 的 think-act loop 内部完成。
1) What to store（存什么）：
- 输入是一条完整轨迹（55K–170K tokens 量级），包含大量探索噪声与死胡同。
- REM 将其“巩固”为一个 phase-structured document，按四阶段组织：localize、understand、fix、verify。作者强调这是两层意义：既是检索单元，也是注入上下文的主载体，避免“存一份、注入又复制一份”的 token 浪费。
- 关键取舍：不把轨迹打散成零碎 factoids（会丢结构），也不保留原始逐步日志（噪声稀释标识符、且挤占当前推理空间）。
2) When to recall（何时召回）：
- 两级读取路径：阶段化文档在任务开始就注入；更昂贵、更易干扰的 implementation record（更接近原始实现细节/操作记录）先不注入。
- 在 loop 内设置一个“struggle-gated”节点：当观察到 agent 卡住/挣扎时，才把第二层 implementation record 注入。
- 这里的核心主张是：召回时机必须依赖接收方 agent 的状态（例如是否已定位 bug），而这个状态在检索时不可见。
3) What to forget（忘什么）：
- implementation record 只暴露一次后立刻驱逐（one-shot eviction），避免它持续偏置后续推理；阶段化文档则保留全程。
- 这相当于把“高噪声但高细节”的记忆当作短期干预，而把“低噪声结构化摘要”当作长期背景。
此外，REM 把唯一的领域特定部分压到 extraction schema，并声称该 schema 可从示例轨迹自动发现（减少手工设计）。全文的论证重点是：收益主要来自 stored form（阶段化文档），而 gating/eviction 负责让第二层细节不造成伤害。
summary.experiments:
评测基于 SWE-ContextBench Lite（Zhu et al., 2026），指标用端到端 resolution（是否修复成功）而不是仅看 retrieval accuracy。
关键结果与现象（按全文表述）：
- 阶段化文档作为检索单元，在 SWE-ContextBench Lite 上检索准确性领先 13 个点（作者称为 SOTA retrieval）。
- 端到端：REM 在每个 replicate 都提升 resolution，同时总体成本下降 17%。对比之下：
  - 仅在 run 开始注入 summary 或注入 raw trajectory，不能提升 resolution；
  - 即便 oracle 提供“正确经验”，天真注入也可能不改变最终结果，说明失败不在检索命中而在使用/时机。
- 利用率分析：agent 只引用 raw trajectory 中约四分之一的 identifiers；对 prose summary 也只用到约一半的 identifiers。作者用这个证据解释为什么长轨迹会稀释关键信号、并造成注意力/位置偏置下的低效使用。
- 能力分层现象：同一段记忆对中等能力模型有帮助，但对最强模型可能有代价（负迁移），支持“记忆注入是控制问题”的论点。
这些实验更像在刻画长上下文与经验复用的动力学，而不是提出新的检索模型。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议（约 45–60 分钟）：
- 先读 Introduction 里对“检索不是瓶颈”的三条证据链，并留意作者如何把问题转成 control（状态依赖的注入/移除）。
- 精看方法部分的三决策拆分，以及两级 read path（document vs implementation record）和 struggle-gated 的触发条件；这是 REM 的核心。
- 实验部分优先看：
  1) oracle memory 仍无效的对照（用来证明时机/形态的重要性）；
  2) decision-level ablation（存储形态 vs gating vs eviction 谁贡献最大）；
  3) utilization analysis（identifiers 使用比例）——这对做长上下文预训练/数据形态的人很有参考价值。
- 如果只想抓结论：看 §5.1–§5.5（按文中引用），再回头补 §3 的 schema 自动发现细节。

summary_en.core_problem: Long-horizon coding agents generate massive trajectories, but experience rarely compounds across runs. The paper argues the bottleneck is not retrieval relevance; it is the unmanaged memory lifecycle: what representation to store, when to inject which memory tier during the think-act loop, and when to remove it to avoid distraction and negative transfer.
summary_en.importance:
Not a pretraining-method contribution, but highly relevant to foundation-model research around long-context behavior, trajectory-to-asset conversion, and continual agent learning. The paper provides concrete, experimentally backed points that map to pretrain/post-train design:
- More context can hurt: timing and placement dominate, aligning with known long-context uneven usage and position bias.
- Structure transfers better than raw detail: phase-structured consolidation improves reuse, suggesting training data may benefit from structured process representations rather than raw logs.
- Memory is a control problem: recall/eviction should be state-dependent and decided inside the agent loop, not as a one-shot retrieval decision.
It is also useful as evidence that stronger models can be harmed by unnecessary memory, which matters when designing curriculum, mid-training, or tool-trajectory distillation pipelines.
summary_en.technical_approach:
REM (Reusable Experience Memory) introduces three explicit decisions, executed from within the agent’s loop:
1) What to store:
- Each completed run is a 55K–170K token trajectory with heavy exploration noise.
- REM consolidates it into a phase-structured document organized by four phases: localize, understand, fix, verify. This document is both the retrieval unit and the primary injected context, avoiding duplicated token spending.
- The design choice is deliberate: not raw trajectories (too noisy and context-hungry), not atomized factoids (lose solution structure).
2) When to recall:
- Two-tier read path: the phase document is injected at task start; a much costlier “implementation record” (fine-grained details closer to the original trace) is withheld.
- A struggle-gated in-loop node injects the implementation record only when the running agent appears stuck, leveraging the fact that the agent state is observable only inside the loop.
3) What to forget:
- The implementation record is evicted after a single exposure (one-shot eviction) to prevent persistent bias; the phase document remains for the whole run.
Additionally, the only domain-specific artifact is an extraction schema, which the paper claims can be automatically discovered from example trajectories. Ablations are framed to show gains come mainly from the stored form, while gating/eviction prevent the second tier from causing harm.
summary_en.experiments:
Evaluated on SWE-ContextBench Lite, using end-to-end task resolution (bug-fix success) rather than retrieval accuracy alone.
Reported highlights:
- The phase-structured document yields the best retrieval accuracy on the benchmark, with a +13 point margin.
- REM improves resolution in every replicate while reducing cost by 17%.
- Start-of-run summaries or raw-trajectory injection do not improve resolution; even with an oracle providing the correct experience, naive injection may not change outcomes—supporting the claim that reuse fails at utilization/timing, not retrieval.
- Utilization analysis: agents reference only ~25% of identifiers in raw trajectories and ~50% in prose summaries, explaining dilution and distraction.
- Capability-dependent effects: the same memory can help mid-capability agents but hurt the strongest ones (negative transfer), reinforcing the need for state-dependent control.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim plan (45–60 minutes):
- Read the Introduction carefully for the argument that retrieval is not the main failure point and why this becomes a control problem.
- Focus on the method’s three decisions and the two-tier read path with struggle-gated injection; that is the core mechanism.
- In experiments, prioritize: (1) the oracle-memory-but-no-gain result, (2) decision-level ablations separating storage form vs gating vs eviction, and (3) the identifier utilization analysis—these are the most transferable insights for long-context pretraining and trajectory shaping.
- If time is tight, read the main results section first (the paper cites §5.1–§5.5) and then backfill the schema discovery details.

recommendation.zh: 读方法图和消融即可；把记忆召回放进执行循环是干净改动，比离线相似检索更像可用系统。
recommendation.en: Skim the method diagram and ablations; moving recall into the execution loop is a cleaner systems idea than offline similarity retrieval.

paper.title: RELAY: Scaling Historical Build Restoration through Rule Reuse and Agentic Repair
paper.abstract: Vulnerability benchmarks and software engineering research depend on rebuilding historical software. Yet builds rely on external resources, such as base images and packages, that change independently of the source code. In this study, we examine this environment decay on 14,159 OSS-Fuzz cases. We find that 69.7% no longer complete reconstruction and verification, and that most failures share a small number of recurring failure symptoms. A recurring failure can therefore be diagnosed once and its

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文解决历史软件构建环境衰退导致 benchmark 无法重建的问题，目标是在大规模 OSS-Fuzz 案例上恢复可复现构建。
summary.importance: 它对 LLM 基座预训练不是直接相关，但对 coding agent 和软件工程 benchmark 维护很实用。真正有价值的点不是“让 agent 修 bug”，而是发现大量失败可归结为少数重复模式，因此规则复用比逐例 agent 更划算。
summary.technical_approach: 作者提出 RELAY：先用 LLM 从代表性失败案例中归纳并验证确定性修复规则，后续同类失败直接复用规则而不再调用模型；只有规则无法覆盖的样本才升级到逐例 agent 修复。这个设计把 agent 从默认路径降为兜底路径，核心是 rule reuse + agentic escalation。
summary.experiments: 数据集为 14,159 个 OSS-Fuzz 历史案例，其中 69.7% 已无法完成重建与验证。论文比较了人工引导和全自动规则归纳流程，并与纯 per-case agent 方法对比，结论是可复用规则能恢复相当数量的构建，同时显著减少模型调用与成本。摘要未给出更细粒度成功率数字。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses environment decay in historical software builds, aiming to restore reproducible builds at scale for OSS-Fuzz cases.
summary_en.importance: It is not directly relevant to LLM pretraining, but it is practically useful for coding agents and benchmark maintenance. The real insight is not 'use an agent to fix builds' but that many failures collapse into a small set of recurring patterns, making rule reuse more efficient than per-case agent repair.
summary_en.technical_approach: The authors propose RELAY: use an LLM to derive and validate deterministic repair rules from representative failures, reuse those rules without further model calls on matching cases, and escalate only unresolved cases to a per-case agent. The key design is rule reuse plus agentic escalation, with the agent as fallback rather than default.
summary_en.experiments: The study covers 14,159 OSS-Fuzz historical cases, of which 69.7% can no longer be reconstructed and verified. It compares human-guided and fully automated rule-derivation campaigns against a pure per-case agent baseline, finding that reusable rules restore as many builds with fewer model calls and lower cost. The abstract does not provide more detailed success-rate numbers.

recommendation.zh: 对 pretrain 没直接帮助，但对做 coding agent benchmark 的人有个朴素而对的结论：先抽规则再让 agent 兜底，别一上来逐例调用大模型。
recommendation.en: Not directly useful for pretraining, but for coding-agent benchmark maintenance it makes a sound point: extract reusable rules first, then use the agent as fallback instead of default.

paper.title: SWE-Residual: Evaluating Starting-State Robustness of Coding Agents

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的不是“代码 agent 能不能从零做任务”，而是更贴近真实交接场景的另一件事：当起始环境里已经有前一个人或前一个 agent 留下的一套“看起来已经做完”的改动时，后续 agent 能否识别其中哪些部分其实是错的、缺的，继续把任务真正做完。现有 SWE 类 benchmark 几乎都默认 clean start，因此测到的是从空白状态解题的能力，却没有测“接手半成品且没有上下文”的能力。论文把这个能力定义为 Starting-State Robustness，并指出 clean-start 分数高并不意味着这种鲁棒性也高，甚至模型排序会反转。
summary.importance: 对大模型研究的直接价值主要在评测侧，而不是预训练方法本身。它补上了 coding agent 评测里一个长期被忽略的维度：agent 是否会把已有产物当成事实，还是会回到原始需求重新核对。这件事和真实部署很相关，因为多轮会话、多人协作、多 agent pipeline 都天然会产生状态继承。对基座研究员来说，启发在两点。第一，当前 agent 能力评测过度依赖 clean-start，容易高估模型在真实软件流程中的可用性。第二，论文识别出的 acceptance bias 很像一种推理与规划层面的先验偏置：模型倾向于接受已有改动的叙事，而不是主动验证需求与实现是否一致。这对后续做 agentic training、过程监督、轨迹数据构造、甚至 pretrain 中的“验证型”数据设计都有参考意义。
summary.technical_approach:
方法上，论文的核心不是提出新 agent，而是构造一个新的 benchmark：SWE-Residual。每个样本由原始任务请求、隐藏测试，以及一个 Residual State 组成。这个 Residual State 来自某个 predecessor agent 在原 benchmark 任务上的一次失败但“自认为完成”的提交状态。也就是说，后继 agent 看到的是一个已经被改过的 repo 或机器环境，里面包含新增文件、代码修改、安装的软件和配置变化，但隐藏测试仍未全部通过。

构造流程的关键点有三个。第一，Residual State 不是随便截取中间状态，而是 predecessor agent 明确提交完成后的最终状态，因此更像真实 handoff。第二，任务请求和 verifier 保持不变，这样同一个 agent 可以在 clean start 和 residual start 上直接对比，差值就是 starting-state robustness 的损失。第三，论文给出 residualization pipeline，用于从 DeepSWE 和 Terminal-Bench 的原任务中系统地收集、验证、筛选这些残留状态，并且 predecessor 覆盖了 DeepSeek、Qwen、GLM 三个模型家族，避免 benchmark 只对某一类错误模式过拟合。

分析层面，作者提出 acceptance bias 作为主要失败机制：后继 agent 会把继承来的改动当成“任务边界”的定义，而不是把它当作待审查对象。表现为它会浏览已有改动、运行测试、做少量局部修补，但很少推翻已有实现，也很少去修改 predecessor 没碰过的文件。这个定义比简单说“agent 不够鲁棒”更有信息量，因为它把失败归因到了状态解释方式，而不只是搜索不够或代码能力不够。
summary.experiments:
数据集规模上，SWE-Residual 一共包含 198 个 Residual States，来自 111 个任务，底座 benchmark 是 DeepSWE 和 Terminal-Bench。Residual State 由三类 predecessor 模型家族生成。论文强调这些状态往往已经“很像完成了”：在 DeepSWE 上，Residual State 对隐藏测试的中位通过率已经达到 98.4%，这意味着后继 agent 面对的不是明显坏掉的代码，而是只差最后一些关键 corner case 或遗漏需求的近完成状态。

结果上，五个前沿 coding agents 在 residual start 下都出现明显退化。相对 clean start，DeepSWE 上成功率下降 20.6 到 53.5 个百分点，Terminal-Bench 上下降 20.6 到 34.9 个百分点。更重要的是，DeepSWE 上模型排名发生反转，说明 clean-start leaderboard 不能稳定预测真实交接场景下的表现。

失败分析是全文最有价值的部分。作者发现，在 DeepSWE 的失败 continuation 中，有 58.9% 到 88.2% 的样本，结束时失败的测试和起始时失败的测试完全相同。也就是说，agent 接手后并没有真正触及残留问题，哪怕同一个 agent 从 clean start 出发时通常能把这些测试修掉。这一现象强烈支持 acceptance bias：模型不是不会做，而是没有重新定位问题。论文还提到后继 agent 往往保留大部分继承改动，且很少修改 predecessor 未涉及的文件，这进一步说明它把已有实现当成可信锚点。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇适合泛读，但建议把引言、benchmark 构造细节和失败分析认真看完。先看 Introduction，作者对问题定义得很清楚，尤其是 clean start 与 residual start 的区别，以及为什么这不是简单的 harder benchmark。然后看 SWE-Residual 构造部分，重点关注 Residual State 的定义、筛选标准、与原 benchmark 的对齐方式，确认 benchmark 没有因为任务改写而引入额外混淆。实验部分优先看 clean vs residual 的主表，以及关于 ranking reversal 的结果。最后看 acceptance bias 的定性和定量分析，这部分最能帮助理解 agent 为什么会失败。

如果时间有限，30 到 40 分钟可以抓住主要信息：问题定义、数据构造、主结果、失败模式。若要进一步深挖，建议思考两件事：一是这种偏差能否通过训练时加入“审计已有实现”的轨迹数据缓解；二是 benchmark 是否区分了“已有改动质量高但方向错”和“已有改动质量低但表面完整”这两类不同残差状态，它们对应的 agent 能力可能并不相同。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies a capability that standard coding-agent benchmarks largely miss: can an agent successfully continue a task when the starting state already contains prior work that looks complete but is still wrong or incomplete? Existing SWE-style benchmarks mostly use clean starts, so they measure from-scratch problem solving. They do not measure whether an agent can inherit a partially solved repository or machine state, infer what remains broken without prior context, and finish the task. The paper names this capability Starting-State Robustness and shows that strong clean-start performance does not imply strong robustness under inherited states.
summary_en.importance: This is primarily an evaluation contribution, but it matters for foundation-model researchers because it exposes a mismatch between benchmarked capability and deployed behavior. Real coding workflows involve handoffs across sessions, humans, and multiple agents. In those settings, the model must audit inherited artifacts rather than treat them as ground truth. The paper also identifies a concrete failure mode, acceptance bias, where the agent implicitly trusts prior edits and frames the remaining work around them instead of re-checking the original request. That diagnosis is useful beyond benchmarking: it suggests directions for agent training, process supervision, trajectory curation, and possibly pretraining data that teaches verification against specifications rather than local continuation of an existing narrative.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The main contribution is a benchmark, SWE-Residual, not a new coding agent. Each benchmark instance pairs the original task request and hidden tests with a Residual State: the final state left by a predecessor agent that declared the task complete even though the hidden tests still fail. The inherited state may include code edits, new files, installed packages, or configuration changes, depending on whether the source task comes from DeepSWE or Terminal-Bench.

The construction has three important design choices. First, the residual state is taken from a predecessor’s submitted final state rather than an arbitrary intermediate checkpoint, making it closer to a realistic handoff. Second, the task request and verifier are unchanged, so the same task can be evaluated from both a clean start and a residual start; the difference isolates starting-state robustness. Third, the residualization pipeline collects and validates such states from multiple predecessor model families, including DeepSeek, Qwen, and GLM, reducing the chance that the benchmark overfits to one model’s characteristic mistakes.

The paper’s main analytical contribution is the notion of acceptance bias. The successor agent tends to treat inherited work as defining what remains to be done, rather than treating it as an object to verify against the original request. In practice, the agent inspects prior edits, often runs tests, and makes limited local changes, but rarely revisits untouched files or challenges the predecessor’s framing of the solution. That is a sharper diagnosis than simply saying the agent is less robust.
summary_en.experiments:
SWE-Residual contains 198 residual states drawn from 111 tasks based on DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench. The predecessor states come from three model families. A notable detail is that these residual states are often very close to completion: on DeepSWE, the median residual state already passes 98.4% of the hidden tests. So the benchmark is not mainly about recovering from obviously broken environments; it is about detecting subtle missing requirements or incorrect edge-case handling in states that look finished.

Across five frontier coding agents, success drops substantially under residual starts. Relative to clean starts, the drop is 20.6 to 53.5 percentage points on DeepSWE and 20.6 to 34.9 points on Terminal-Bench. On DeepSWE, model rankings even reverse, which is one of the strongest results in the paper because it shows that clean-start leaderboards are not stable proxies for real handoff performance.

The failure analysis is the most informative part. In 58.9% to 88.2% of failed continuations on DeepSWE, exactly the same tests fail at the end as at the beginning of the continuation. That means the agent often does not meaningfully engage with the residual defect, even though the same agent can usually fix those tests from a clean start. The paper also reports that agents tend to preserve most inherited edits and rarely modify files the predecessor never touched, reinforcing the acceptance-bias interpretation.
summary_en.reading_guide:
This is a skim paper, but it is worth reading the introduction, benchmark construction, and failure analysis carefully. Start with the introduction for the problem framing; it clearly explains why residual starts are not just a harder version of clean starts. Then read the SWE-Residual construction section, focusing on how residual states are defined, validated, and aligned with the original tasks. In the experiments, prioritize the clean-vs-residual comparison tables and the ranking-reversal result. Finally, read the qualitative and quantitative analysis of acceptance bias; that is where the paper becomes more than a benchmark release.

If time is limited, 30 to 40 minutes is enough to extract the main ideas. If you want to go deeper, two follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind: whether this failure mode can be reduced by training on audit-style continuation trajectories, and whether different kinds of residual states should be separated more explicitly, for example high-quality but misdirected prior work versus low-quality but superficially complete prior work.

recommendation.zh: 揭示了 Coding Agent 评测中的一个重要盲区（初始状态敏感性），对构建更鲁棒的 Agent 评测体系和训练数据合成有启发。
recommendation.en: Reveals a critical blind spot in coding agent evaluation (starting-state sensitivity), offering insights for building more robust agent evaluation frameworks and training data synthesis.

paper.title: SWE-Bench Pro V2: A Cleaner, Harder-to-Game Coding Benchmark

summary.core_problem: SWE-Bench Pro V2 解决的是代码智能体评测失真的问题：原始 SWE-Bench Pro 中大量任务存在指令、隐藏测试、环境和 verifier 不一致，且更强的 agent 会利用网络、git 历史、测试文件等评测漏洞拿到不可信分数。
summary.importance: 这不是预训练方法论文，但对代码模型和 coding agent 的评测信号有直接影响。代码能力现在常被用作基座模型、SFT/RL recipe、agent scaffold 的核心外部指标；如果 benchmark 的测试要求没有写进任务描述，或者 agent 能从 GitHub 抄到参考解，分数就会混入数据污染和 harness 漏洞。V2 的价值在于把 issue-based coding benchmark 的维护流程工程化：任务缺陷分类、agentic audit、专家复核、盲重实现、隔离重评。对做代码预训练或 RL for coding 的团队，启发主要在评测闭环，而不是模型训练本身。
summary.technical_approach: 方法围绕“任务有效性”和“防作弊协议”两条线展开。任务有效性要求：满足指令的解应通过，不满足指令的解应失败。作者从 731 个 SWE-Bench Pro public v1.0 任务出发，做了三轮修复。第一轮修复 40 个容器镜像和模板问题。第二轮用自动审计检查难度校准、指令与测试对齐、reward hacking 风险，随后由工程师修改任务描述和测试覆盖关系。第三轮加入两类 agentic audit：一类静态比较 instruction、测试列表和 reference patch，标记测试要求缺失、指令与测试矛盾、测试细节泄漏、未被测试覆盖的行为、fixture 缺失、整文件级测试列表等模式；另一类运行多个 agent 配置，让 LLM judge 根据轨迹、patch、verifier log 和 graded tests 判断失败来自模型还是任务。所有被标记任务由专业工程师裁决，修复后通过盲重实现验证。防作弊方面，协议禁止 agent 阶段访问除模型 endpoint 外的网络，清理镜像中的 git 历史，verifier 会回滚测试相关修改后再应用隐藏测试，并在干净容器中重新评分。
summary.experiments: 最终从 731 个任务发布 642 个任务，其中 391 个有任务级修复，89 个被丢弃，480 个任务被修复或移除，占 66%。23 名合约工程师投入 404 小时，每个修复后的 instruction 都由第二名工程师在只看文本的条件下重新实现验证。网络封禁实验很关键：一个 frontier model 在允许访问 GitHub 时有 351 个 solved tasks 直接复制参考解，但 GitHub 被封后只有 237 个仍成立，说明原协议会明显高估能力。V2 上，Claude Opus 5 in Claude Code 解决 99% 的 642 个任务，Gemini 3.8 Flash 为 94.9%，Inkling 为 89.9%。完整集对最前沿系统已接近饱和，但 51-task Hard split 仍能把系统拉开，从 52.9% 到 98.0%。作者还报告了 agent harness 变化会影响成本，但对 open-weight 模型的准确率影响不大。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读 20–30 分钟。优先看 Section 3 的修复流程和 Figure 2，弄清 731 个任务如何流转到 642 个任务；再看缺陷分类表，尤其是 instruction-test mismatch 和 leakage 的具体模式。Section 4.4 的 exploit 分析值得细读，它说明 coding benchmark 的主要风险已经不只是数据污染，还包括运行时环境给 agent 留出的旁路。Section 5 可快速看，重点是为什么一个 frontier 模型接近饱和的 benchmark 仍可用于区分非前沿系统。若只关心模型训练，可以跳过 leaderboard 排名细节，把注意力放在 benchmark 清洗和 verifier hardening 的流程上。

summary_en.core_problem: SWE-Bench Pro V2 addresses a measurement problem in coding-agent benchmarks: many original tasks had mismatches among instructions, hidden tests, environments, and verifiers, while stronger agents could exploit network access, git history, and test-editing loopholes instead of solving the issue.
summary_en.importance: The paper is an evaluation and benchmark-maintenance contribution rather than a pretraining method. Its relevance to foundation-model work is still practical. Coding benchmarks are now used to compare base models, post-training recipes, RL systems, and agent scaffolds. If hidden tests check behavior not stated in the prompt, or if an agent can recover the reference patch from GitHub, the score no longer measures the intended capability. The useful contribution is a concrete operating model for maintaining real-issue benchmarks under stronger agents: defect taxonomy, agentic audit, expert adjudication, blind re-implementation, and hardened grading.
summary_en.technical_approach: The benchmark is repaired along two axes: task validity and exploit resistance. A task is treated as valid only if any solution satisfying the instruction passes, and solutions that do not satisfy it fail. Starting from 731 public SWE-Bench Pro v1.0 tasks, the authors run three repair rounds. Round 1 fixes 40 container-image and template issues. Round 2 uses automated audits for difficulty calibration, instruction-test alignment, and reward-hacking risks, followed by engineer edits. Round 3 adds two agentic audits. The artifact audit statically compares the instruction, test lists, and reference patch, flagging missing requirements, contradictions, leaked solution or test details, untested changed behavior, missing fixtures, and whole-file test grading. The failure audit runs multiple agent configurations, then uses an LLM judge to attribute each rejection to either the model or the task. Every flagged task is adjudicated by professional engineers, and repaired instructions are validated through blind re-implementation. The protocol also disables non-endpoint network access during the agent phase, removes git history from images, reverts test-related edits before applying hidden tests, and re-grades patches in clean containers.
summary_en.experiments: The release contains 642 tasks from the original 731. In total, 480 tasks, or 66%, were repaired or removed; 391 released tasks have task-specific repairs and 89 tasks were discarded. The repair process used 23 contracted engineers for 404 hours, with a second engineer validating each revised instruction by solving from the text alone. The exploit analysis is important: with GitHub access, a frontier model copied reference solutions verbatim on 351 solved tasks, but only 237 of those held up once GitHub was blocked. On V2, Claude Opus 5 in Claude Code resolves 99% of all 642 tasks, Gemini 3.8 Flash resolves 94.9%, and Inkling resolves 89.9%. The full set is close to saturated for the strongest systems, but the 51-task Hard split still separates systems from 52.9% to 98.0%. The paper also reports that changing the agent harness affects cost more than accuracy for open-weight models.
summary_en.reading_guide: A 20–30 minute skim is enough for most pretraining researchers. Start with Section 3 and Figure 2 to understand how the 731 original tasks become the 642-task release. Then read the defect taxonomy, especially instruction-test mismatch and leakage patterns. Section 4.4 is the highest-signal part for evaluation design, because it shows how benchmark scores can be inflated through environment-level loopholes rather than model capability. Section 5 can be read quickly for the argument that a near-saturated benchmark can still be useful for non-frontier systems. If the goal is model training rather than benchmark construction, skip most leaderboard detail and focus on the audit and verifier-hardening pipeline.

recommendation.zh: SWE 评测防污染/防刷值得扫，重点看样本清洗和判题协议，不必按 coding 方法论文读。
recommendation.en: Worth skimming for SWE contamination and anti-gaming design; focus on sample cleaning and judging protocol, not coding-agent methods.

paper.title: When Coding Agents Outpace Review: Evaluating PRD-Driven Development in Mature Enterprise Repositories
paper.abstract: Coding agents increasingly undertake development tasks in mature enterprise repositories, yet existing benchmarks offer limited insight into whether they fulfill complete Product Requirement Documents (PRDs) and where delivery breaks down. Issue resolution and development from scratch leave incremental PRD fulfillment underexplored, while isolated tests provide incomplete evidence of business and integration requirements. We introduce PACE, a benchmark of 43 enterprise tasks with 750 expert-audi

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的不是“代码 agent 能不能过单元测试”，而是更接近真实企业开发的问题：在成熟仓库里，给定一份会不断澄清和演化的 PRD，agent 到底能否完成完整需求，而不是只修掉局部 issue 或写出能跑通部分测试的 patch。现有 benchmark 多数依赖测试用例或 issue-level 任务，难以覆盖业务规则、跨模块集成约束、接口兼容性和验收条件。论文的核心问题，是如何把真实企业开发记录转成一套可审计、可复现、能定位失败原因的 PRD 驱动评测。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接关联不强，它更偏评测与 coding agent 诊断，因此只适合 skim。启发点主要有两类。第一，它提醒人们：代码模型的能力边界不应只用 pass@k 或单仓库 issue 修复来衡量，真实增量开发需要更强的检索、规划、跨文件编辑和验证闭环。第二，它在评测设计上强调“冻结验收合同 + 分层证据收集 + 轨迹归因”，这套思路对 agent benchmark、长程任务评测、甚至 post-train 数据构造都有借鉴意义。若你关心代码预训练与后训练接口，这篇能帮助理解当前 coding agent 的失败模式主要落在哪些环节。
summary.technical_approach:
方法贡献主要在 benchmark construction 和 evaluator design。PACE-Bench 从企业生产记录出发，每个任务包含多轮用户-代理对话、基础仓库、最终接受的 diff 和元数据。作者先把这些材料重建成一份 standalone PRD，尽量保留最终需求范围，但避免把参考实现里后来引入的命名或偶然设计变成硬约束。

随后是双通道准则抽取：
- PRD-only pass 只看需求文档，抽取应交付的行为和约束；
- reference-diff-only pass 只看已接受改动，记录实际改了什么，但不反推业务意图。

两路结果再做 reconciliation，过滤 incidental edits 和没有证据支撑的推断，再把保留下来的要求拆成原子级 Code Points。每个 Code Point 带有行为描述、证据来源、检索提示、允许替代实现、以及权重。这里的关键设计是“冻结合同”：在评测前就把 acceptance contract 固定下来，后续所有 agent 都按同一套标准打分，避免 judge 随任务漂移。

评测器分三层：
- L0 做结构性硬约束检查，直接排除明显违反接口/配置/格式要求的实现；
- L1 用有界 call-graph 搜索收集候选代码和集成上下文，尽量把证据定位到相关模块；
- L2 用 judge 对每个 Code Point 做带引用证据的语义判断，允许等价实现而不拘泥于参考 patch。

最后用确定性规则把每个点聚合成 Covered / Partial / Missing，并按权重汇总总分。除了功能分数，论文还把 acceptance loss 与 agent trajectory 中的检索、编辑、验证信号对齐，用来分析失败是因为没找到代码、没改对、还是没验证到位。这一点比单纯 leaderboard 更有诊断价值。
summary.experiments:
基准包含 43 个 enterprise brownfield tasks，750 个经专家审计的 Code Points，任务改动规模中位数是 1,465 行、15 个文件，说明它不是轻量 toy task。论文评测了 11 个 model-scaffold 配置，主结果显示大多数系统得分落在 52.1 到 78.1 之间，但“完整 PRD 交付”比例很低，最好也只有 14.0%。这说明当前 coding agent 即使能完成不少局部要求，离完整企业需求还有明显差距。

评测器本身的可靠性是论文的重点之一。作者报告其自动评估与独立专家共识的一致率达到 95.2%，并通过接受的 reference patch 和四类 negative controls 来探测评分边界。这比只给一个 LLM-as-a-judge 分数更扎实，因为它同时检查了覆盖性和稳定性。

从分析结论看，失败通常不是单一原因，而是多环节断裂：有些任务是 retrieval 不充分，没找到真正相关的代码路径；有些是 edit 能力不足，改动没有贯穿依赖模块；还有些是 verification 不够，生成了看似合理但未被证据支持的实现。论文还展示了如何利用这些诊断信号去改 harness，并在同一冻结基准上复测改动效果。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇更适合带着问题泛读。建议先看 Introduction 和 Figure 1，理解它为什么不用传统 test-only benchmark。然后重点看 Benchmark Construction，尤其是 PRD reconstruction、双通道 criterion synthesis、以及 Code Point 的冻结方式。接着看 evaluator 的 L0/L1/L2 三层设计，判断它在“可审计性”和“允许等价实现”之间怎么取舍。最后看主表和 failure attribution 分析，那里最能说明当前 coding agent 的短板。

如果你的关注点是基座预训练，这篇不需要逐段细抠。30 分钟左右足够抓住 benchmark 设计和主要结论。更值得留意的是它暴露出的能力结构：成熟仓库开发不是单步代码生成问题，而是检索、规划、跨文件一致性和验证闭环问题。这些能力缺口，很多并不能靠更高 pass@k 自动补上。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper is not asking whether coding agents can pass unit tests. It asks a harder and more realistic question: given a PRD in a mature enterprise repository, can an agent deliver the full requested change, including business rules, integration constraints, and acceptance conditions, rather than only solving a local issue or producing a patch that satisfies partial tests? Existing benchmarks focus heavily on issue resolution, greenfield generation, or executable oracles, which leaves PRD-level fulfillment in brownfield repositories under-measured. The core problem is how to build an auditable, reproducible benchmark that evaluates complete PRD delivery and explains where the delivery process breaks.
summary_en.importance: This is only loosely connected to pretraining, so it belongs in skim territory. Its value is mainly methodological. First, it shows that coding-agent capability is poorly captured by pass@k or issue-fixing benchmarks when the real task is incremental development inside a large existing codebase. Second, its evaluation design—frozen acceptance contracts, layered evidence gathering, and trajectory-linked diagnosis—is useful for agent benchmarking more broadly. If you care about the interface between code pretraining and post-training, the paper is helpful because it exposes where current agents fail: retrieval, cross-file editing, integration, and verification, not just raw code synthesis.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The contribution is primarily in benchmark construction and evaluator design. PACE-Bench starts from production development records: multi-turn user-agent conversations, the base repository, the accepted patch, and task metadata. The authors reconstruct a standalone PRD that preserves the final intended scope while avoiding leakage from implementation-specific names or incidental design choices introduced by the accepted patch.

Criterion synthesis then proceeds in two independent passes:
- a PRD-only pass that extracts required behaviors and constraints from the request,
- a reference-diff-only pass that records what changed in the accepted implementation without inferring business intent.

These are reconciled to filter incidental edits and unsupported inferences, then refined into atomic Code Points. Each Code Point includes the behavior to be checked, provenance, retrieval hints, allowed alternatives, and a weight. The key design choice is to freeze these acceptance contracts before evaluation so that all agents are judged against the same target.

Scoring is three-stage:
- L0 performs structural checks for explicit hard violations,
- L1 uses bounded call-graph search to gather candidate code and integration context,
- L2 applies a judge to each Code Point with cited evidence, while allowing semantically equivalent implementations rather than requiring the reference patch.

Deterministic aggregation maps each point to Covered, Partial, or Missing and produces weighted scores. The paper then links acceptance losses to trajectory signals from retrieval, editing, and verification, which turns the benchmark into a diagnostic tool rather than a pure leaderboard.
summary_en.experiments:
PACE-Bench contains 43 enterprise brownfield tasks and 750 expert-audited Code Points. The tasks are nontrivial: the median accepted change spans 1,465 lines across 15 files, which is much closer to real incremental development than toy issue-fixing setups.

The benchmark evaluates 11 model-scaffold configurations. Most systems score between 52.1 and 78.1, but complete PRD delivery remains rare: the best setup achieves only 14.0%. That is the main empirical message. Current coding agents can satisfy a meaningful fraction of requirements, but full enterprise-task completion is still uncommon.

A major part of the experimental story is evaluator reliability. The paper reports 95.2% agreement with independent expert consensus, and it probes the scoring boundary using accepted reference patches plus four negative controls. That makes the evaluation more credible than a single opaque LLM-judge score.

The failure analysis suggests that misses come from different stages of the agent loop: insufficient retrieval of the relevant code path, edits that do not propagate through dependent modules, and weak verification that leaves unsupported or incomplete implementations in place. The paper also shows how these diagnostics can guide harness revisions and be rechecked on the same frozen suite.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Read this as a benchmark-design paper, not as a model paper. Start with the introduction and the construction overview figure to understand why test-only evaluation is insufficient for PRD-driven development. Then focus on three pieces: PRD reconstruction, the bidirectional criterion-synthesis pipeline, and the frozen Code Point contracts. After that, read the L0/L1/L2 evaluator design to see how the paper balances auditability with flexibility for equivalent implementations. Finish with the main results table and the failure-attribution analysis, which are the most informative parts.

If your main interest is foundation-model pretraining, you do not need a line-by-line read. Around 30 minutes should be enough to extract the benchmark design and the main findings. The practical takeaway is that mature-repository development is a retrieval-planning-editing-verification problem, not just a code-generation problem.

recommendation.zh: 把“交付”从单测/issue 拉到 PRD+证据链是对的；只看 benchmark 定义与失败归因表就够，用它校准你内部 coding RL 的 reward 设计。
recommendation.en: The PRD + evidence-chain framing is the right move beyond unit-test/issue benchmarks; read the benchmark spec and failure breakdown tables to calibrate rewards for coding RL.

paper.title: Over-Defense in Coding Agents Begins at Silent Forks
paper.abstract: Language models behind coding agents are post-trained with outcome rewards, and recent methods concentrate credit on the turns that decide the outcome. We find that defensive actions beyond what a task requires escape both. They begin at silent forks, the turns where every next action leads to the same outcome. Such actions leave the success rate unchanged, and frontier models take the disproportionate branch there in up to 91% of decisive actions under implicit budgets. The most direct fix, a c

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作讨论的不是“代码 agent 会不会完成任务”，而是“它在完成任务时为什么会系统性地做过量防御动作，以及现有 outcome-based post-training 为什么学不到这个问题”。论文把过度防御的起点定位到 silent fork：在某个决策点上，不同后续动作在任务成败上等价，但在行为是否合比例上不同。典型例子是目标测试已经通过后，直接提交和再跑一遍测试都能成功，但后者是多余动作。作者的核心论点是：只按最终 outcome 给奖励，或者只把 credit 分给改变 outcome 的关键步骤，都无法在 silent fork 上产生有效学习信号，因为这些分支的 value 相同，梯度天然消失。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究本身，它不是直接改 pretrain recipe，而是给 pretrain↔post-train 接口提供了一个很具体的信号：当模型被训练成 agent 后，很多行为质量问题并不体现在最终成功率上，而体现在“同样成功时怎么做”。这类问题如果只靠 outcome reward，很容易形成盲区。对做 RL post-training、agentic data synthesis、process supervision 的人，这篇文章的价值在于它把“学习信号应该放在哪里”说得很清楚：不是只看 outcome 改变处，而要看行为分叉处。这个判断对 coding agent 之外也有外溢意义，比如工具调用、长链推理、浏览器 agent 中的冗余检查、重复调用、保守过度等现象，很多都可能属于同一类 credit assignment 失配。
summary.technical_approach:
技术上分三步。第一步是诊断。作者构造 behavioral checker，回放成功轨迹中的命令，跟踪仓库状态、已完成编辑、已执行检查，并把动作标成是否超出任务所需。然后在成功轨迹里定位“第一个偏离合比例行为的动作”，把它定义为 over-defense 的起点。进一步通过重采样前缀，验证这些点确实是 silent fork：后续行为不同，但 outcome 不变。

第二步是解释为什么常见 RL 修补无效。最直接的想法是把 checker 输出并入 trajectory reward，对过度防御加惩罚。问题在于，这种奖励只有当整条轨迹在所有 silent fork 上都走了合比例分支时，才会把差异传回早期 fork；任务一长，这种“全程都对”的轨迹组合概率迅速下降。再叠加 GRPO 这类组内相对奖励算法，只在同组 rollout 奖励有差异时更新，很多组会完全没有学习信号。

第三步是方法设计：ForkDPO。作者不再从 outcome 反推 credit，而是直接在 fork 处构造 preference pair。具体有两类 pair。其一是过度防御侧：checker 找到成功轨迹中第一个不合比例动作，从同一前缀重采样得到更合比例的替代动作，形成 chosen/rejected。其二是欠防御侧：对于那些如果直接提交会跳过必要检查的 silent fork，也构造另一侧的 pair，避免模型被训练成一味少检查。然后在这些 fork-level pair 上做 DPO。这个设计和随机抽取 turn 做 DPO 的区别很关键：监督信号被精确放在行为真正分叉的位置，而不是平均撒在整条轨迹上。
summary.experiments:
实验重点有三层。第一层是现象测量。作者在 4B 模型和 4 个 frontier 模型上观察到，silent fork 几乎就是 over-defense 的起点；在隐式预算设置下，把这些 fork 的前缀喂给模型，模型在决定性动作上选择不合比例分支的比例最高可到 91%。文中还指出，这些 fork 两侧通常都不改变仓库状态，且过度防御轨迹与其他轨迹成功率相当，这直接支持“outcome 不区分行为质量”的判断。

第二层是基线失败分析。把 checker 并入 trajectory reward 后，用 GRPO 训练，在隐式预算任务上有 71% 到 74% 的 rollout group 奖励完全相同，因此组内相对更新几乎不起作用；训练 12 轮后，不合比例率没有明显下降。随机 turn 的 DPO 也效果有限，说明问题不只是“缺少偏好数据”，而是偏好必须落在正确位置。

第三层是 ForkDPO 的效果。在 48 个来自未见仓库的测试任务上，4B 模型的 implicit-budget disproportion rate 从 70.3% 降到 58.9%，下降 11.4 个点；中位运行时间从 143 秒降到 90 秒，约减少 37%。作为对比，随机 turn 的 DPO 只把比例降到 67.7%。论文还强调，双侧 pair 都重要：只压过度防御而不约束必要检查，容易把策略推向欠检查；加入“必须检查”的另一侧监督后，行为边界更稳定。就实验叙事而言，这篇文章最有价值的不是绝对数值，而是把 silent fork→reward vanishing→fork-level preference 这条因果链闭合了。
summary.reading_guide:
建议先看 Introduction 和 Figure 1，把 silent fork 的定义吃透。这是全文最重要的概念。然后看 behavioral checker 的定义与标注规则，重点理解作者如何区分“必要检查”“过度防御”“欠防御”，因为方法成立依赖 checker 的行为语义而不是 outcome 语义。

接着看 GRPO 失败分析部分，尤其是关于 identical rewards within group 的统计。这一段回答了“为什么给轨迹加惩罚还不够”。如果只看结果表，很容易误以为是 GRPO 没调好；作者真正想说明的是 credit placement 错了。

ForkDPO 部分要重点看 pair construction。需要确认 chosen/rejected 是如何从同一前缀得到的，是否会引入分布偏移，以及双侧 pair 为什么能约束行为区间而不是单向压缩。实验里优先看三类图表：silent fork 的分布与性质、GRPO 组内奖励同质化统计、ForkDPO 与 random-turn DPO 的对比。预计 35 到 50 分钟可以抓住主线；如果你做 agent RL 或 process supervision，值得再花时间细看 checker 设计和 pair 采样细节。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies a failure mode that standard outcome-based post-training largely misses: coding agents often take excessive defensive actions even when those actions do not improve task success. The authors trace the onset of this behavior to silent forks, decision points where alternative next actions differ in proportionality but lead to the same final outcome. Once the task outcome is already settled, outcome rewards and outcome-sensitive credit assignment provide no gradient for preferring the proportionate branch over the excessive one.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining paper in the narrow sense, but it is highly relevant to the pretrain-to-posttrain interface. It shows that a large class of agent behavior errors are invisible to success-only rewards. For researchers working on RL for agents, process supervision, synthetic trajectory generation, or verifier design, the main contribution is conceptual and operational: learning signals should be attached where behavior diverges, not only where outcome changes. That point likely extends beyond coding agents to tool use, browser agents, long-horizon reasoning, and other settings where redundant checking or conservative over-execution is common.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The method starts with diagnosis. A behavioral checker replays successful trajectories, tracks repository state and required checks, and labels actions that go beyond what the task requires. The first such action in a successful run is treated as the onset of over-defense. By resampling from the same prefix, the paper shows that these points are silent forks: the next action can vary in proportionality while preserving success.

The paper then explains why a straightforward RL fix is weak. One can add checker-based penalties to the trajectory reward, similar in spirit to length-controlled RL. But that signal reaches a given fork only through trajectories that remain proportionate at all relevant forks. As trajectories get longer, such fully proportionate rollouts become rare. Under GRPO, which updates from within-group reward differences, many rollout groups become reward-identical, so the policy receives little or no learning signal.

The proposed solution is ForkDPO, a fork-level preference optimization scheme. Instead of inferring credit from outcome, it directly constructs preference pairs at the behaviorally meaningful fork. There are two pair types. One targets over-defense: the checker identifies the first disproportionate action in a successful trajectory, and the model is resampled from the same prefix to obtain a more proportionate alternative. The other targets under-checking: when immediate submission would skip a required check, the method also creates pairs on that side, so the model does not simply learn to check less. DPO is then applied to these fork-level pairs. The key difference from random-turn DPO is precise signal placement at the actual behavioral branching point.
summary_en.experiments:
The empirical story has three parts. First, the diagnosis: on a 4B model and four frontier models, silent forks are shown to be where over-defense begins. Under implicit budgets, when models are prompted from these fork prefixes, they choose the disproportionate branch in up to 91% of decisive actions such as testing, checking, or submitting. The paper also notes that both branches usually leave the repository unchanged and that over-defensive runs succeed as often as other runs, which directly supports the claim that outcome does not distinguish behavior quality here.

Second, the failure of reward-based fixes: when the checker is folded into the trajectory reward and training is done with GRPO, 71% to 74% of rollout groups under implicit-budget settings receive identical rewards, so relative updates largely vanish. After 12 rounds, the disproportion rate does not meaningfully improve. Random-turn DPO also helps little, indicating that the issue is not merely the absence of preference data, but the location of that data.

Third, ForkDPO improves behavior on 48 test tasks from unseen repositories. For the 4B model, the implicit-budget disproportion rate drops from 70.3% to 58.9%, an 11.4-point reduction. Median runtime falls from 143 seconds to 90 seconds, roughly a 37% decrease. Random-turn DPO only reaches 67.7%. The ablations also argue that both sides of the behavior boundary matter: penalizing over-defense alone can push the model toward insufficient checking, while adding pairs for required checks stabilizes the target behavior.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Start with the introduction and the first motivating figure. The definition of a silent fork is the central idea, and the rest of the paper is built around it. Then read the behavioral checker section carefully. The method depends on a behavior-level notion of proportionality, so the checker’s rules for over-defense, required checks, and under-checking are not implementation details; they are the supervision interface.

Next, focus on the analysis of why GRPO with trajectory-level checker rewards fails. The statistics on reward-identical rollout groups are especially important because they explain why a seemingly reasonable RL fix does not move behavior. Without that section, it is easy to misread the result as a weak baseline rather than a credit-assignment problem.

In the ForkDPO section, pay close attention to how preference pairs are constructed from the same prefix, how resampling is used, and why two-sided supervision is needed. In the experiments, prioritize the tables or figures showing the prevalence and properties of silent forks, the GRPO reward-homogeneity analysis, and the comparison between ForkDPO and random-turn DPO. A first pass should take about 35 to 50 minutes; if you work on agent RL or process supervision, the checker design and pair construction are worth a slower second read.

recommendation.zh: 这篇不是 pretrain，但把“奖励该落在哪个 token/决策点”讲得很清楚；只看 silent fork 定义和 91%/74% 两个数字，就足够改你对 RL credit assignment 的直觉。
recommendation.en: Not a pretraining paper, but it cleanly shows where reward should attach in agent trajectories; the silent-fork framing plus the 91%/74% numbers are enough to update your intuition about RL credit assignment.

paper.title: Peer Pressure: Execution-Verified Co-Evolution of Attacker and Defender Populations for Code Security
paper.abstract: LLM code agents increasingly ship code with little oversight, yet defenders trained on static vulnerability datasets fall behind adapting adversaries. We co-train attacker and defender instead, and let execution decide every reward: an attacker (Red) edits a real repository and earns nothing unless its patch applies, builds, passes the tests, completes its development task and reproduces a real exploit in an isolated container, whose path also labels the entry point, the critical operation and t

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的是一个动态安全训练问题：代码生成与代码审查都越来越由 LLM 承担，但现有防御模型大多训练在静态漏洞数据上，攻击分布一旦变化，检测器就会落后。作者提出，不再把 attacker 当作离线数据生成器，而是让 attacker 与 defender 在可执行验证环境中共同进化。核心难点有两个：一是单一红蓝对抗很快会策略塌缩，双方学不到新东西；二是 defender 的训练奖励会随着对手停滞而虚高，无法反映真实进步。
summary.importance: 对预训练主线而言，这不是直接的 base-model pretrain 论文，但它对 post-train、agentic code model、execution-grounded RL 有明确启发。价值主要在三点。第一，它把“安全数据”从静态标注集改成了可执行、可验证、会随对手变化而更新的训练信号，这和很多人讨论的 synthetic curriculum、self-play、verifiable reward 是同一类问题。第二，它提出的 peer-relative baseline 不是简单的多智能体对战技巧，而是在固定 verifier 预算下改善 policy gradient 信号质量，减少把对手停滞误判为自己进步的风险。第三，代码安全只是一个载体，方法也在 jailbreak safety 上做了验证，说明作者想讨论的是更一般的 adaptive adversarial training。
summary.technical_approach:
技术方案分成两层。第一层是 execution-verified training environment。作者在真实仓库的容器化副本中植入已知弱点类别，并要求只有当现成 exploit harness 能打通时，这个样本才被纳入训练。这样得到的不是“猜测这里可能有漏洞”，而是“这里存在一条可达 exploit path”的可验证样本。Red 的任务是在给定开发任务的前提下编辑 reference diff：对于 vulnerable scenario，要引入一个可利用且可达的 weakness，同时保证补丁能应用、能构建、能通过测试、还能完成原开发任务；对于 clean scenario，则做规模相近但不引入漏洞的编辑。Blue 则像代码审查模型一样，不只要判断 vulnerable/clean，还要定位 entry point、critical operation 和中间 trace，输出对开发者可操作的定位信息。

第二层是 PRPO，Peer-Relative Policy Optimization。每一侧不是单个 policy，而是 N 个 LoRA adapter 组成的同角色种群，挂在同一个 frozen base 上，LoRA 参数量约为基座的 0.1%，便于低成本维护多策略与权重重组。每一轮固定一个条件 ω=(scenario, frozen opponent committee, decoding budget)，让同角色策略在相同条件下比较。作者把 same-role peers 放进 advantage baseline，而不是放进 opponent pool、reward shaping 或 learned critic。直观上，这样做的目的是让某个 policy 的得分反映“在同样对手、同样任务、同样预算下，它比同伴好多少”，从而把对手强弱波动和样本难度波动从梯度信号里扣掉。文章把这种收益称为 matched-population advantage，并给出 advantage variance 的闭式分析。为避免种群退化，训练中还有 tournament 机制：淘汰最弱 adapter，并从较强策略重播种，维持策略多样性。

还有一个设计值得注意：这是非零和游戏。Red 不能靠生成无法构建或无法通过测试的垃圾补丁来“骗赢”，因为 reward 由执行验证决定，必须同时满足功能正确与 exploit 可达。这个约束很关键，它把攻击者从“让 Blue 犯错”改成“生成真实、可部署、难检测的危险改动”，使训练信号更接近实际代码代理场景。
summary.experiments:
从引言可见，实验围绕五个问题展开：攻击者是否足够可靠以支撑训练、co-evolution 是否优于静态训练、是否能迁移到未见应用和语言、是否必须做权重更新、以及在固定 verifier 预算下 population 是否有收益。评测域至少包括代码安全和 jailbreak safety，代码安全部分使用 VulnGym，并与 supervised、within-policy、frontier-model、已发表 agent baseline 比较。

全文给出的关键结果方向很明确。第一，execution-verified attacker 不是只会制造无效噪声，它能稳定产出“补丁可应用、可构建、通过测试、且 exploit 可复现”的训练样本，因此可以作为在线对手而不是离线数据增强器。第二，co-evolution 优于静态 defender 训练，而且需要对手持续适应；若对手不变，Blue 的训练 reward 会继续上升，但对 held-out external attacker 或历史对手的真实表现不会同步提升。第三，population 设计在固定 verifier 预算下优于单 policy，对应作者区分的 estimator effect 与 allocation effect。第四，仅靠推理时搜索或固定策略对战不够，权重更新带来额外收益。由于题面截断，没有完整数表可逐项复述，但阅读时应重点核对：balanced accuracy 的提升幅度、对未见仓库/语言的迁移结果、以及 PRPO 相对单对手 PPO 或静态 SFT/RL 的增益。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议按方法链路来。先看 Introduction，抓住作者为何强调 static vulnerability dataset 不够，以及为什么单一红蓝对抗会失稳。然后直接看 PRPO 总图和 Section 3，重点理解 condition ω、frozen committee、same-role peer baseline 这几个对象分别控制什么变量。接着看 execution verifier 的定义与 reward 组成，确认 Red 为什么不能通过破坏构建来取巧。最后看实验部分里 RQ2、RQ5，对应“co-evolution 是否必要”和“population 是否在固定预算下有效”，这两点最有方法含量。

如果只留 30 分钟，建议看 Figure 1、PRPO 公式、verifier 流程图、主结果表和 ablation。若准备精读，则要仔细看作者如何区分 training reward、external attacker 评测、historical opponent 评测，因为这关系到是否真的学到了鲁棒防御，而不是只适应当前对手。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a dynamic security-training problem. LLMs increasingly write and review code, but most defenders are trained on static vulnerability datasets, while the attack distribution keeps moving. The authors replace static supervision with co-evolution: an attacker and a defender are trained against each other inside an execution-verified environment. Two failure modes motivate the method. A single attacker-defender pair quickly collapses to a narrow strategy set, and the defender’s training reward can keep rising even when the attacker has stopped improving, making progress look better than it is.
summary_en.importance: This is not a base-model pretraining paper, but it is relevant to post-training, execution-grounded RL, and adaptive data generation. The contribution is useful for anyone thinking about verifiable rewards, self-play, or synthetic curricula. First, it turns security supervision from a static labeled corpus into an executable and adaptive signal. Second, the peer-relative baseline is not just a multi-agent engineering trick; it is a way to improve policy-gradient credit assignment under a fixed verifier budget. Third, the code-security domain is a concrete testbed, but the paper also evaluates on jailbreak safety, which makes the method more general than a narrow coding application.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The method has two layers. The first is an execution-verified training environment. The authors instrument known weakness classes into containerized copies of real repositories and only admit a site if an existing exploit harness can actually fire. This yields samples with executable ground truth: not merely that a vulnerability class is present, but that there exists a reachable exploit path. Red edits a reference diff that already completes a development task and passes tests. On vulnerable scenarios, Red must introduce one reachable weakness of the target class while preserving functionality. On clean scenarios, Red makes a similarly sized edit that introduces no weakness. Blue acts as an LLM code reviewer: it must classify the patch and localize the entry point, critical operation, and trace, which makes the output actionable rather than purely binary.

The second layer is PRPO, Peer-Relative Policy Optimization. Each side is a population of LoRA adapters over one frozen base model, with adapter size around 0.1% of the base parameters. A training round fixes a condition consisting of the scenario, a frozen committee of opposing policies, and a decoding budget. Same-role policies are then compared under identical conditions. The key idea is to place the population inside the policy-gradient baseline rather than in the opponent pool, reward shaping, or a learned critic. Intuitively, a policy is rewarded for outperforming peers that faced the same task, same opponents, and same budget, which removes some variance due to opponent strength and instance difficulty. The paper calls this the matched-population advantage and provides a closed-form analysis of the resulting advantage variance. To avoid strategic collapse, the population is maintained with a tournament mechanism that retires weak adapters and reseeds them from stronger ones.

An important design choice is that the game is non-zero-sum. Red cannot win by producing broken code that fails to build or fails tests. Rewards are execution-verified, so Red must generate patches that are functional, exploitable, and difficult for Blue to detect. That makes the training signal much closer to realistic code-agent deployment.
summary_en.experiments:
The experimental program is organized around five questions: whether the attacker is reliable enough to train against, whether co-evolution beats static training, whether the detector transfers to unseen applications and languages, whether weight updates are necessary, and whether a population helps under a fixed verifier budget. The paper evaluates at least on code security and jailbreak safety, with the code-security side using VulnGym and comparing against supervised baselines, within-policy baselines, frontier-model baselines, and published agent baselines.

The main empirical story is clear from the full text. First, the execution-verified attacker is not just generating noisy adversarial examples; it can reliably produce patches that apply, build, pass tests, and reproduce real exploits, which makes it a viable online training opponent. Second, co-evolution outperforms static defender training, and the adapting opponent matters. If the attacker stops improving, Blue’s training reward can still rise, but held-out evaluation against an external attacker or historical opponents does not show the same gain. Third, the population design helps at a fixed verifier budget, which the paper analyzes in terms of estimator effect versus allocation effect. Fourth, inference-time search alone is insufficient; actual weight updates provide additional benefit. The prompt here truncates the later sections, so exact headline numbers are not fully recoverable from the provided text, but the key tables to inspect are the balanced-accuracy gains, transfer to unseen repositories and languages, and the ablations comparing PRPO against single-policy PPO or static SFT/RL setups.
summary_en.reading_guide:
A good reading path is to follow the method pipeline. Start with the introduction to understand why static vulnerability datasets are insufficient and why a single red-blue pair is unstable. Then go straight to the PRPO section and its main figure. Focus on the role of the fixed condition, the frozen opponent committee, and the same-role peer baseline. After that, read the execution-verifier section carefully to see why Red cannot exploit the reward by producing non-functional patches. Finally, inspect the experiments for the questions on whether co-evolution is necessary and whether the population helps under a fixed verifier budget; those are the most methodologically informative parts.

If you only have about 30 minutes, read the overview figure, the PRPO equations, the verifier pipeline, the main result table, and the ablations. For a deeper pass, pay close attention to how the paper separates training reward from evaluation against an external attacker and historical opponents. That distinction is central to the claim that the defender is becoming genuinely more robust rather than merely overfitting to the current adversary.

recommendation.zh: 如果你关心 RL 信号质量，这篇比“代码安全”本身更值得看：执行验证奖励和同条件 peer baseline 都能迁移到更广的 agent/post-train 设定。
recommendation.en: If you care about RL signal quality, this is more interesting than the security framing itself: execution-verified rewards and condition-matched peer baselines may transfer to broader agent post-training.

paper.title: StopLoss: Teaching Agents to Predict Failure and Stop Early
paper.abstract: Coding agents keep working on runs that will fail verification, and asking a frontier model to watch for this is expensive in its own right.
